result.title: SciFig2Data: A Workflow for Recovering Structured Data from Scientific Figures
result.summary: Scientific measurements reported in scholarly articles are often embedded in compound figures rather than available as machine-readable data. Recovering these measurements at literature scale requires an integrated workflow for figure localization, panel decomposition, chart identification, numerical reconstruction, and experimental context association. We present \textit{SciFig2Data}, an automated, high-throughput workflow for harvesting structured experimental data from scientific PDF repositories. The system integrates multi-scale document element detection, adaptive compound figure decomposition, two-stage OCR-based semantic filtering, Swin-based chart classification, and instruction-guided multimodal large language model (MLLM) reconstruction. It further incorporates directory-level batch execution, caching, and structured logging to support large-scale processing. We demonstrate the workflow on two biomedical literature corpora comprising 605 toxicology and pharmacology articles and 551 lipid nanoparticle (LNP) articles. The pipeline successfully reconstructed 468 and 242 tabular outputs from the respective corpora, illustrating its practical applicability to literature-scale scientific data harvesting. By associating reconstructed measurements with caption-derived experimental metadata, SciFig2Data provides a workflow for transforming graphical evidence in scholarly publications into structured, context-enriched data records for downstream AI4Science applications.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 SciFig2Data 自动化流程，从科学论文 PDF 中定位复合图、拆分子图、分类图表，并用指令引导的 MLLM 将图中数值重建为结构化表格数据。
AI.relevance_reason: 属于文献数据抽取的工程流水线，MLLM 仅一次性地把图表转写为表格，不涉及推理期 latent 状态、视觉证据筛选或多步推理决策，与 LVR 主线缺少可核查的状态、训练或停止机制联系。
